That leaves 26.75 credits, so before committing to those two runs I want to do one 96B run first (16 credits) at lr=0.0002, wd=0.035, near the predicted optimum, to refine the fit and reduce uncertainty in the wd direction where extrapolation is riskiest — the lr exponent uncertainty is small enough (±4% at 4x extrapolation) not to worry much about. I'll run that 96B point now, then refit before launching the 384B pair.

The refit on the 6B–96B data fits nearly within seed noise and predicts the 384B optimum near lr 0.000102, wd 0.048, with sharp wd curvature. I'll run one more 96B trial near its predicted optimum to confirm the trend, then two 384B runs bracketing that predicted wd at the predicted lr.

The two loss values are consistent with the model, both close to optimum. I'll refit including this point, then plan two 384B runs at the optimal learning rate (~0.000102), bracketing weight decay values around 0.040 and 0.058 to cover the predicted 0.048-0.053 range.

Actually, since the wd optimum depends on lr with rho ~0.7-1, even if my chosen lr is slightly off from the true optimum, the measured wd optimum at that lr is still what matters, so I'll proceed with lr = 0.000102 based on the fits converging around 0.000101-0.000104. I'll refit quickly with the new data point and then launch both 384B runs in parallel, using cost 128 out of the remaining 10.75 budget.
